extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, proofreaders, compositors, and publishers (University of Chicago Press and similar editorial offices)
extracted.subtask_description: A publisher's typographical and editorial style manual (University of Chicago Press, 4th ed., 1914) giving rules and examples for composition and production of printed works (capitalization, italics, quotations, spelling, punctuation, divisions, footnotes, indexing, tabular work, technical terms, and specimens of type).

rubrics_metrics.name: Introductory guidance on application of rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations are meant for the average case and must be applied with a certain degree of elasticity; exceptions may legitimately be made according to subject-matter, argument emphasis, author's preference, or typographical contingency; deference should generally be shown to the expressed wishes of the author where no question of taste or logic is involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules point the way rather than operate as unchanging law; applicability in the printing-office and common-sense are preferred over rigid consistency; local conditions and kinds of publications can call for modification; anomalies and deviations are noted in the body of the Manual; specimen pages of available types and special characters are provided for manufacturing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and function of the Manual
rubrics_metrics.description: A codification of typographical rules employed by the University of Chicago Press intended to govern publications issued with the Press's imprint; not exhaustive and not inflexibly consistent, but intended as practical working rules for typographical form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Manual includes specimen pages of types and special characters; changes and periodic revisions reflect literary practice and profession developments; adoption by other editorial offices and libraries is noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization (general rules and lists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules for when to capitalize in English composition, enumerated across many numbered items (e.g., proper nouns and adjectives; epithets; particles in foreign names; geographic generic terms; regional adjectives; political divisions; names of thoroughfares; political parties; religious denominations; official titles; ordinals; historical epochs; events; conventions; treaties; creeds; civic holidays; titles of honor; abbreviations; divine names; acquired special meanings; personifications; Bible and sacred book usages; first words in sentences and certain enumerations; titles of publications; foreign-title rules; and many more).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each numbered rule gives specific examples and many exceptions (e.g., 'Capitalize proper nouns and adjectives: George, America, Englishman' but 'Do not capitalize verbs derived from proper names: to boycott'); lists of place-name generic terms which are capitalized when part of the organic name and not when used descriptively; treatment of particles in French, Dutch, German names; when to capitalize political/body names versus generic references; capitalization rules for titles, headings, and foreign-language titles with language-specific guidance (Latin, French, German, Dutch, etc.); treatment of scientific names; special usages for the Bible, parables, and sacred terms; date-line and salutatory formatting using caps and small caps; explicit numbered exceptions and notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of italics
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules specifying when to italicize words, phrases, foreign words, emphasis, short foreign passages, and other special uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Italicize words or phrases to which emphasis or importance is to be lent; italicize foreign-language words or phrases inserted in English text and not incorporated into English (examples: 'the Darwinian Weltanschauung', 'coup d'etat'); single sentences or brief foreign passages not long enough to be set in reduced type are italicized. The Manual also lists exceptions (e.g., do not italicize foreign titles preceding names) and gives further detailed guidance in subsequent numbered items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for handling quotations within printed text, including punctuation, capitalization, block quotations vs. run-in quotations, and related formatting conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Manual provides rules about when the first word of a quotation is capitalized (connected quotations vs. independent sentences), punctuation placement with quotation marks, treatment of quotations after colons and in enumerations, and how to set long quoted passages (reduced type, indention). Specific numbered rules and examples are provided in the Quotations section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on preferred spellings, orthographic conventions, treatment of variants, and possibly recommended American/British choices as applied by the Press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Spelling section (listed in the contents) includes the Press's recommended spellings and discussion of changes in spelling practice; the Manual emphasizes 'progressive conservatism' rather than radical reform in spelling. (Section contains explicit lists and examples; consult the Spelling section for details.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing punctuation marks (commas, semicolons, colons, periods, dashes, hyphens, quotation marks, parentheses, etc.) and their typographical usage in printed works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Punctuation section provides many specific rules and examples for punctuation usage, including complex cases such as punctuation with quotations, enumerations, clauses, and parenthetical material; also rules for punctuation in titles, headings, and lists. (See Punctuation section for numbered guidance and examples.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisions (heads, sections, enumeration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for dividing text: headings, subheads, sections, enumerations, and the capitalization/formatting rules applying to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Manual prescribes treatment of cap-and-small-cap and italic center-heads, bold-face cut-in heads and side-heads, cap-and-small-cap box-heads in tables, and rules about capitalization within headings; it gives formatting recommendations (try to avoid center-heads; indention rules for certain cases) and numbered examples (see items about first words in enumerations, first words after colons, numbering conventions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes and notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for the use, formatting, numbering, and placement of footnotes and notes in publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Manual contains a Footnotes section describing how to number notes, placement of references, typographical conventions for footnote text (type size, indention), treatment of 'NOTE' headings (set in small capitals and followed by period and dash in notes), and examples of correct layout. (Refer to Footnotes section for detailed numbered rules.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on compiling and formatting indexes: what to include, entry forms, subentry treatment, and typographical conventions for indexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Indexing section gives rules for form of entries, use of small capitals or capitals, handling of cross-references, and conventions for page-numbering and subheads. Examples and specimen index forms are provided to guide indexers and editorial staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabular work
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for composing tables: heading capitalization (cap-and-small-cap box-heads), column heads, alignment, and numeric and textual conventions within tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Tabular Work section prescribes use of cap-and-small-cap or italic heads in tables, which words in heads to capitalize, alignment of numbers and text, rules for footnotes within tables, and recommended spacing and borders; see numbered pages and figures for specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: A glossary or section of technical/field-specific terms and their typographical treatment and abbreviations as used in Press publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Technical Terms section addresses specialized vocabulary, conventions of abbreviation, treatment of foreign technical terms, and how to render scientific names and units; explicit examples (e.g., Latin names, units) and language-specific rules are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Hints to authors and editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical recommendations to authors and editors on preparing copy to conform to Press standards and to ease production (submission format, bibliographies, references, manuscript preparation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Hints to Authors and Editors' appendix contains actionable guidance for authors (manuscript preparation, bibliographic formats) and editors (preferred styles for citations and references), with examples. It supplements the main rules by offering pragmatic tips to avoid common production problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Hints to proofreaders and copyholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions and best practices for proofreaders and copyholders on catching and correcting typographical and editorial errors, and how to apply the Manual's rules in proofing and copy-setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate 'Hints to Proofreaders' and 'Hints to Copyholders' sections give checklists, common error types, and recommended approaches; they coordinate with the 'Proofreader's Marks' chart provided elsewhere in the appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreader's marks
rubrics_metrics.description: A standardized set of proofreader's marks and symbols to indicate corrections, insertions, deletions, and typographical adjustments in proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Manual prints the conventional marks (with examples) to be used on proofs to communicate needed corrections to compositors; the chart assists uniform interpretation across editorial and manufacturing staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens of types (manufacturing guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimen pages showing the available typefaces, sizes, cut styles, ornaments, initials, borders, and other decorative devices used by the Press to guide composition and design decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimen pages show many typefaces (Scotch Roman, DeVinne, Gothic, Jenson, Tiffany, etc.) at multiple point sizes, with sample text and numerals; ornaments, borders, initials, and the university coat-of-arms are included for selection and production reference. These specimens inform choices of typeface, point size, emphasis, and ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting of letters and formal salutations (use of caps and small caps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for setting the town/state in the date line, salutatory phrase, signatures, and institutional names in letters and articles, including use of caps and small caps and recommended alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'CHICAGO, ILL., January 1, 1911' set to the right with one em indention and in smaller type; 'MY DEAR MR. SMITH:' set flush followed by colon and in the same type as body; signatures set to the right; institutional names and addresses set in caps and small caps and centered lines. Specific indention and type-size recommendations are provided.
